title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：saucer　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 saucer 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the baker ① washed the saucer that no customer in the bakery would have counted, and he said the washing was the whole of the week. The ② saucer, meaning the dish itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed uncounted in the book; a saucer, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ saucer in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ saucer at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A saucer, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the baker said the counting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the saucer was the whole of the matter, meaning the care and not the dish. The ⑥ saucer, meaning the care and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; saucer, he said, is either something you wash or the only word that means both a dish and a care. He said the care is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ saucer had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ saucer of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of counting; saucer, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ saucer I remember is the dish counted in the bill, which closed in 1964 and is still counted as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ saucer, my mother said in 1966, is the only dish that improves by being counted; every saucer, she said, is a care that has agreed to look like a dish. She said the care was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 茶碟（指糕饼铺里每一只旁边的那一只）
B. n. 茶碟（指那只茶碟本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：wash the saucer 洗这一只茶碟
D. n. 茶碟（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 茶碟之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的茶碟之事）
F. n. 茶碟（指账单里写到、被清点的那一只）
G. n. 茶碟、讲究（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 讲究（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: washed the saucer that no customer in the bakery would have counted
The saucer, meaning the dish itself and not the tray
the saucer at the far oven

A saucer, my mother said in 1966

answers.why: wash the saucer 意为“洗这一只茶碟”，1957 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯清点的一只茶碟做了一遍。
saucer 意为“茶碟”，指那只茶碟本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被清点。
saucer 意为“茶碟”，指糕饼铺里每一只旁边的那一只，每一只旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
saucer 意为“茶碟”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
saucer 意为“茶碟、讲究”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这只讲究就是那件事的全部。
saucer 意为“讲究”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那只茶碟，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
saucer 意为“茶碟”，指账单里写到、被清点的那一只，到 1962 年这一只成了账单里的一行。
saucer 意为“茶碟之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的茶碟之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的清点。
saucer 意为“茶碟”，我记得的是账单里清点过的那一只，1964 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一只。
saucer 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，茶碟是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的茶碟。
